finding.text: When several landed tasks share the same number of words, the tie goes to the most expensive one (`b.l.usd - a.l.usd`, TaskQueue.js:28). That pushes estimates up: in check-after.txt row 20, "Remove the All sessions back link" (a one-line change) is estimated at $20.76. A neutral tie-break, such as the most recent task or the original order, would not lean high.

`TaskQueue.words` keeps every word of 4 or more letters, so filler words like "with", "that", "make", "every" and "sessions" count as shared words. Two shared words is then easy to reach, and loosely related tasks get matched (TaskQueue.js:15). A short stop-word list would make the matches tighter. This is a tuning question; the build is correct.

The deliverable number: the top 20 had 4 distinct scores before (0.745, 0.497, 0.373, 0.248; the brief guessed 1 or 2) and 11 after (check-before.txt, check-after.txt). The ten 0.745 rows that tied at the top are now spread out.

Ask 2 said to check that `--check` prints the landed titles. It doesn't print them. They are clearly filled in, though, because the estimates now differ between rows (check-after.txt). The smoke line from `smoke.mjs` isn't saved in the task folder, so I couldn't confirm that the page loads cleanly.
